decisive_items: Monomorphic, perivascular, and periadnexal atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
Phenotypically abnormal T-cell population with CD52 expression
CD3-positive T cells coexpressing CD4 and CD8 with preserved expression of CD7
response.rationale: Skin biopsies show atypical lymphocytic infiltrate with abnormal T-cell phenotype, diagnostic of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Behçet's disease is supported only by oral/genital ulcers but lacks the characteristic histopathology.

rejected.why: Ulcer morphology is nonspecific; biopsy shows atypical lymphocytes, not neutrophilic infiltrate typical of pyoderma gangrenosum.
Oral/genital ulcers are present but histopathology and immunophenotype point to a T-cell neoplasm, not Behçet's.
Same as R1; duplicate Behçet's label without additional support.
Vasculitis is suggested by purpura and inflammation, but biopsy shows atypical lymphocytic infiltrate with fibrin thrombi, more consistent with lymphomatous vasculopathy.
